pages: 2-Stage Outdoor Unit (Cooling Only) EcoNet Codes The error codes below will be displayed at the EcoNet Control Center under Service window / Current Faults or in the Fault History and will be time & date stamped. Codes listed in the center column will show on the outdoor control board’s seven segment display. EcoNet error code at Control Center A950_O Configuration Data Restore Failure A951_O Memory Card Config Data Write Failure T952_O Outside Temp Thermistor Failure T957_O Low Refrigerant Pressure A957_O Low Refrigerant Pressure T958_O High Refrigerant Pressure Display on Unit Description   The firmware in the outdoor unit control board is corrupt. Replace control board.   Missing, loose or corrupt memory card  The outdoor temperature thermistor is connected to the outdoor unit control board. This sensor is mounted below  control box (from factory) or may have been relocated by installer.  Verify connection and wiring of sensor to outdoor control board.  Verify resistance/temperature using 10k@77 degree scale.  Low pressure switch has tripped.  Verify subcooling, superheat, check refrigerant charge.  Ensure indoor expansion valve is operating properly.  Check for frozen or dirty indoor coil  Make sure indoor blower is running and airflow is correct.  System locked out due to T957_O Low Refrigerant Pressure occurring 3 times in a call for operation.  System High Pressure switch tripped.  Check Outdoor Fan motor operation  Verify system is not overcharged  Check cleanliness of outdoor coil.  Liquid Line/Drier Restriction A958_O High Refrigerant Pressure   System locked out due to T958_O High Refrigerant Pressure occurring 3 times in a call for operation. A959_O High Voltage Brown Out  Incoming line voltage is either too low to start or has dropped  while unit is running.  Verify wire sizes are appropriate  Check connections in disconnect, unit and breaker panel

EcoNet Codes (Continued) 2-Stage Outdoor Unit (Cooling Only) T960_O Compressor Locked Rotor A960_O Compressor Locked Rotor - Lockout   Compressor is pulling excessive / locked rotor amps.  Verify run capacitor and plug harness.  Compressor is tight or seized.  Occurs after 3 attempts to restart after T960_O Compressor  Locked Rotor faults.  Verify run capacitor, harness plug,  Compressor is tight or seized. A961_O No Voltage At Compressor   Contactor should be pulled in as control voltage is being sent to it. Check wiring to contactor both line and control voltage.  Faulty contactor coil or contacts. A962_O Compressor Voltage At Standby   Compressor current detected when contactor should be open.  Check for mis-wired plug harness or welded contactor. Additional Troubleshooting Tips: A Blown outdoor fuse will result in no compressor operation only. Board will remain powered and outdoor fan will run with no faults. If contactor is not pulled in, and there are no faults. Verify 3 amp fuse on the control board is not open. This fuse protects the control board from a shorted contactor only. The operational codes listed below will be displayed only on the outdoor unit control board’s seven segment display and represent normal operation. Operational Code displayed on seven segment LED Function    System in stand-by mode  No call for operation  System call for y1 (Low Cool) operation only  Flashing  System call for y1 (Low Cool) operation – Time delay  Anti-short cycle delay active   System call for Y1+Y2 (High Cool) operation  Flashing  System call for Y1+Y2 (High Cool) operation – Time delay  Anti-short cycle delay active
